name: Yokohama Chinatown
why: Japan's biggest Chinatown, ten minutes' walk from the ballpark: ornate gates, the Kanteibyo temple, steamed buns on every corner. Pre-game dinner sorted.
tips: Kanteibyo temple is lit at night
Street food beats the sit-down 'all you can eat' places

name: Sankeien Garden
why: A silk merchant's garden of 17 historic buildings moved here from Kyoto and Kamakura, including a 500-year-old pagoda on a hill over a pond. Early autumn color in November.
tips: Bus from Yokohama station or Motomachi

name: Shin-Yokohama Raumen Museum
localName: 新横浜ラーメン博物館
why: A recreated 1958 Tokyo street in a basement with ramen shops from all over Japan. Order mini bowls and try three styles.
tips: Mini bowls let you sample several shops

name: Cup Noodles Museum
localName: カップヌードルミュージアム
why: Design your own cup noodle and watch it sealed. Silly and genuinely fun.

name: Red Brick Warehouse & Osanbashi Pier
why: 1910s customs warehouses turned shops and bars, with the wooden Osanbashi pier next door for a sunset view of the bay.
tips: Osanbashi pier roof deck is free and open late
mapsQuery: Red Brick Warehouse & Osanbashi Pier, Yokohama, Japan

name: Yamate Bluff & Motomachi
why: Hilltop Western-style houses from Yokohama's treaty-port days, a foreigners' cemetery, and the Harbor View Park lookout.

name: Yokohama Park & Stadium area
why: Before Game 1, walk around the stadium: BayStars blue everywhere, food stalls, and the fan shops on Yokohama Park's edge.
tips: BayStars official store at the stadium gates
mapsQuery: Yokohama Park & Stadium area, Yokohama, Japan

name: Yoshimuraya, Yokohama
why: The 1974 birthplace of iekei ramen. Long line, fast turnover, worth it once.
tips: Buy a ticket at the machine; tell them noodle firmness

name: Manchinro, Chinatown
why: Since 1892, Chinatown's grand old Cantonese house. Dim sum lunch is the affordable way in.

name: Edosei pork buns, Chinatown
why: Huge steamed pork buns to eat walking. Cheap, filling, game-day fuel.
mapsQuery: Edosei pork buns, Chinatown, Yokohama, Japan

name: Noge izakaya alleys
why: Hundreds of cheap izakaya and standing bars in a gritty postwar neighborhood near Sakuragicho. Where Yokohama actually drinks.
tips: Great after a game: 15 minutes' walk from the stadium

name: Gyunabe Araiya, Kannai
why: Yokohama was where Japan first ate beef in the 1860s. Gyunabe (beef hot pot) here since 1895.

name: Motomachi bakeries & patisseries
why: Motomachi's European-style shopping street of old bakeries and patisseries, a reminder of Yokohama's treaty-port days.

name: Chinatown mango and sesame balls
why: Fried sesame balls, egg tarts, mango shaved ice: the Chinatown dessert crawl.

name: Kissaten around Kannai
why: Old-school coffee houses (kissaten) dot the arcades around Kannai station: hand-drip coffee, thick toast, quiet. Pick whichever has a wooden counter and an older owner.

name: Coffee at the Red Brick Warehouse
why: Harbor-side coffee with the bay view.
mapsQuery: Coffee at the Red Brick Warehouse, Yokohama, Japan

name: Yokohama Brewery
why: Yokohama was home to Japan's first commercial brewery (1869). This craft brewpub keeps the tradition: their pilsner and a restaurant upstairs.

name: BayStars beer at the ballpark
localName: ベイスターズ・ビール
why: The BayStars sell their own original craft beers inside Yokohama Stadium. Drink blue.

name: Sirius Sky Lounge, Landmark Tower
why: 70th-floor bar with the bay, the Ferris wheel and Mt. Fuji on clear days. One drink at sunset.
mapsQuery: Sirius Sky Lounge, Yokohama Royal Park Hotel

name: Yokohama Central Wholesale Market
why: A working wholesale fish market with a few public restaurants in the related-goods building. Breakfast sushi without Tokyo's lines.
mapsQuery: Yokohama Central Wholesale Market, Yokohama, Japan

name: Sky Spa Yokohama
why: Baths and saunas on the 14th floor above Yokohama station, with city views. Good for a post-flight or post-game soak.

name: Great Buddha of Kamakura (Kotoku-in)
why: A 13 m bronze Buddha sitting in the open air since 1252. You can go inside it for ¥50.
tips: 25 min by Enoden from Kamakura station, or walk from Hase
mapsQuery: Great Buddha of Kamakura (Kotoku-in), Kamakura, Japan

name: Hase-dera Temple, Kamakura
why: A hillside temple with a sea view, caves of carved deities and a gold Kannon. Five minutes from the Great Buddha.

name: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, Kamakura
why: The shoguns' shrine at the top of Kamakura's main avenue. Komachi-dori street food on the way up.

name: Hokoku-ji bamboo grove, Kamakura
why: A quiet Zen temple with a bamboo grove and a tea house where you sip matcha looking into it. Fewer people than Kyoto's.
mapsQuery: Hokoku-ji bamboo grove, Kamakura, Kamakura, Japan

name: Enoshima Island
why: A small island shrine, caves and sea views, reached by causeway. Fresh shirasu (whitebait) bowls are the local dish.
tips: Take the Enoden train from Kamakura: 25 min of coastal views
